record.original_question: If A is a strict GKK matrix, meaning a P-matrix whose almost principal minors satisfy A[α,β]A[β,α] > 0 for every pair α,β of equal size with dispersal 1, must A be positive stable, i.e. must every eigenvalue of A lie in the open right half-plane? More specifically, if A is both strict GKK and a τ-matrix, must A be positive stable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$. For index sets $\alpha, \beta \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ of equal cardinality, write $A[\alpha,\beta]$ for the minor of $A$ with rows indexed by $\alpha$ and columns indexed by $\beta$. Define the dispersal of the ordered pair $(\alpha,\beta)$ to be $|\alpha \setminus \beta| = |\beta \setminus \alpha|$; minors with dispersal $1$ are called almost principal.

A matrix $A$ is called a $P$-matrix if all of its principal minors are positive. A $P$-matrix $A$ is called a strict GKK matrix if for every pair $(\alpha,\beta)$ of index sets of equal size with dispersal $1$, the almost principal minors satisfy
$$A[\alpha,\beta]\, A[\beta,\alpha] > 0.$$

A matrix $A$ is called a $\tau$-matrix if for every nonempty $\alpha \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}$, the smallest real eigenvalue of the principal submatrix $A[\alpha,\alpha]$ is at least the smallest real eigenvalue of $A$ itself (i.e., the principal submatrices satisfy a monotonicity property of the smallest eigenvalue).

A matrix $A$ is called positive stable if every eigenvalue of $A$ has strictly positive real part.

Questions:
(a) Must every strict GKK matrix be positive stable?
(b) Must every matrix that is simultaneously a strict GKK matrix and a $\tau$-matrix be positive stable?
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that while it is known that not all (non-strict) GKK τ-matrices are positive stable (counterexamples by Holtz and others disproved several conjectures of Carlson, Engel–Schneider, Varga, and Hershkowitz), the analogous questions for the strict GKK class (and for strict GKK τ-matrices) are listed among the open problems on GKK τ-matrices and do not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable
status_evidence.snippet: A class of unstable GKK τ-matrices was described, disproving conjectures of Carlson, Engel & Schneider, Varga, and Hershkowitz.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples exist for general GKK τ-matrices, but these counterexamples are not strict GKK, leaving the strict-GKK stability question open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on GKK tau-matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems on GKK τ-matrices, including stability of strict GKK matrices and strict GKK τ-matrices.
status_evidence.claim: The stability of strict GKK matrices and strict GKK τ-matrices is explicitly listed as an open problem.
